sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Al–Zn binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset AlZn-93Mey-LB.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L → (Al) + (Zn), lies at 380.8 °C.
The Al–Zn system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as simple eutectic, solid miscibility gap, monotectoid.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of S. an Mey, Z. Metallkd., 84, 451-55(1993). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
For Al, the liquidus meets the axis at 660.3 °C.
For Zn, the liquidus meets the axis at 419.5 °C.
The eutectic reaction L → (Al) + (Zn) is calculated at 380.8 °C, with L at x(Zn) = 0.884.
The dataset places a eutectoid ((Al)2 → (Al)1 + (Zn)) at 277.2 °C; the composition of (Al)2 is a mole fraction of 0.590.
The upper stability limit of (Al) is 660.3 °C.
The solubility of Al in (Zn) reaches a mole fraction of 0.031 at 380.8 °C.
At 1000 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its maximum, 2616 J/mol, at x(Zn) = 0.500.
For the equiatomic liquid at 1000 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −3.99 kJ/mol.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
